ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is the torque-speed curve of an induction motor, the vertical axis is labeled Torque, the horizontal axis is labeled Speed, and speed to the right is positive; the vertical axis is labeled 0, indicating the zero-speed position. Four operating points W, X, Y, and Z are marked on the curve, where W is located to the left of the vertical zero-speed axis, that is, in the negative speed region; X, Y, and Z are located on the right side in the positive speed region. Reasoning: The slip of an induction motor s = (Ns - N) / Ns, where Ns is the positive synchronous speed and N is the rotor speed. If s > 1, then Ns - N > Ns, therefore -N > 0, that is, N < 0. That is to say, slip greater than 1 corresponds to operation at negative rotational speed. The marked point in the negative speed region in the figure is W, so the answer is W.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: a torque-speed curve with speed increasing to the right and the zero-speed line at the vertical axis; W is located at negative speed. From the question, we need the marked point with slip greater than 1. Apply s = (Ns - N)/Ns. Since s exceeds 1 only when N is less than 0, choose the marked point in the negative-speed region, W.
